T: Two backpackers. One very local pub.
D: Two American backpackers are attacked by a werewolf on the Yorkshire moors.
P: Serve the snacks when they walk into the Slaughtered Lamb.
S: Dry-brined pork rind roasted until blistered and crisp, with flaky salt
Pork rind scored, salted and dried in the fridge overnight, roasted at 240C for 30 minutes until blistered and crisp, broken into pieces.
Soft boiled eggs wrapped in sausage, crumbed and fried, with English mustard
Eggs boiled 6 minutes, peeled, wrapped in seasoned sausage mince, rolled in flour, egg and panko, fried at 170C for 7 minutes. Hot English mustard.
David wakes up naked in the wolf enclosure at the zoo

Almonds, cashews and peanuts roasted in egg white, brown sugar, rosemary and cayenne until crunchy, with a scatter of flaky salt. Whisk 1 egg white until frothy. Toss with 150g almonds, 150g cashews and 150g peanuts. Mix 60g brown sugar, 1 tbsp chopped rosemary, half a tsp cayenne and 1 tsp salt and toss through. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 150C for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes. Cool completely so they crisp, then sprinkle with flaky salt.
M: a pub table on the Yorkshire moors

Thick-cut vintage cheddar and honey leg ham with crusty bread and salted butter, pickled onions, piccalilli, apple and a pork pie cut into wedges. Slice 300g vintage cheddar into thick slabs and 300g honey leg ham. Cut 1 large pork pie into 4 wedges. Quarter 2 crisp apples. Slice a crusty loaf thickly. Arrange everything on a big board with 80g salted butter, a small bowl of pickled onions, 150g piccalilli, a handful of cos lettuce and cherry tomatoes. Serve with a pint for those who want one.
Lamb mince in tomato and Worcestershire gravy under baked mashed potato
Lamb mince browned with onion, carrot, tomato paste, Worcestershire and stock, simmered 40 minutes, topped with buttery mash and baked at 200C until golden.
W: Baked jam roll pudding served with hot custard
Suet pastry rolled with raspberry jam and baked, served hot with custard. Mix 250g self-raising flour, 125g shredded suet or cold grated butter, 30g sugar and 150ml water into a dough.
K: Keep off the moors mulled ale
English ale warmed with spices and orange, with brandy stirred in

English ale warmed gently with brown sugar, cinnamon, cloves, orange and a splash of brandy, served steaming in heavy glass mugs. Pour 4 x 500ml bottles English ale into a saucepan. Add 3 tbsp brown sugar, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 2 strips orange peel and a grating of nutmeg. Heat gently for 10 minutes, keeping it well under a simmer so the alcohol stays. Stir in 80ml brandy. Strain into 4 heatproof mugs and serve steaming.

s.note: Dry-brined pork rind roasted until blistered and crisp, with flaky salt
s.how: Score 600g pork rind, rub with flaky salt and dry uncovered in the fridge overnight. Roast at 240C for 30 minutes until blistered and crisp all over. Cool for 5 minutes and break into pieces. Stay on the road.

s.note: Soft boiled eggs wrapped in sausage, crumbed and fried, with English mustard
s.how: Boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Wrap each in 100g seasoned sausage mince. Roll in flour, 1 beaten egg and 100g panko. Fry at 170C for 7 minutes. Halve and serve with English mustard.

m.note: Lamb mince in tomato and Worcestershire gravy under baked mashed potato
m.how: Brown 750g lamb mince. Add a diced onion and 2 carrots, then 2 tbsp tomato paste, 2 tbsp Worcestershire and 250ml stock and simmer 40 minutes. Top with 1kg potatoes mashed with 60g butter and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

w.note: Baked jam roll pudding served with hot custard
w.how: Mix 250g self-raising flour, 125g shredded suet or cold grated butter, 30g sugar and 150ml water into a dough. Roll to a rectangle, spread with 200g raspberry jam, roll up and bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Serve with 500ml hot custard.

d.n: Keep off the moors mulled ale
d.note: English ale warmed with spices and orange, with brandy stirred in
d.how: Pour 4 x 500ml bottles English ale into a saucepan. Add 3 tbsp brown sugar, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 2 strips orange peel and a grating of nutmeg. Heat gently for 10 minutes, keeping it well under a simmer so the alcohol stays. Stir in 80ml brandy. Strain into 4 heatproof mugs and serve steaming.
